trust_decision.summary: An IO-backed FBuffer starts as a 512-byte stack buffer (type STACK, capa 512); on the first growth the io fast path promotes it to a heap block of FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE (16383) and then returns on `requested < fb->capa` without accounting for the fb->len bytes already buffered from the stack buffer, so the append that triggered the growth writes up to fb->len bytes past the new heap allocation. The published fix decides this in one place: io buffers are initialised heap-only (capa 0, initial_length = FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE) and the growth loop sizes for requested + fb->len.

landing_point.why: The summary says the heap buffer overflow happens while streaming to an IO, so an engineer looks at the generate path that takes an io VALUE; this is where the io is stored into the FBuffer and where the 512-byte stack_buffer is declared (the same block is duplicated at generator.c:1866-1876).

fix_sites.entry_point: initialisation used by every FBuffer user: JSON::State#generate(obj, io), JSON::State#_generate_no_fallback(obj, io) (generator.c:1314) and JSON::State.generate(obj, opts, io) reached by JSON.dump and JSON::Coder#dump (generator.c:1876)
same as above - fbuffer_realloc is the only allocation path for the generator's output buffer
same as above - fbuffer_do_inc_capa is the capacity check reached from every fbuffer_append* used by the generator
JSON::State#generate(obj, io) and JSON::State#_generate_no_fallback(obj, io) (cState_generate at generator.c:1335)
JSON::State.generate(obj, opts, io) (cState_m_generate at generator.c:1889), reached by JSON.dump(obj, io) at lib/json/common.rb:958 and JSON::Coder#dump(obj, io) at lib/json/common.rb:1080

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fbuffer.h is a private helper (static functions) that also serves the non-IO string/float/indent writers, so a solver can argue the report is about the generator and that the fix belongs where the io enters (generator.c's two FBuffer initialisations) - which is enough to close the reachable crash without touching the shared capacity maths.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The IO contract must stay byte-identical and referentially transparent: State#generate(obj, io) and JSON.dump(obj, io) return the same io object and write exactly the string the non-IO path returns, with partial flushes allowed at each growth; the non-IO path must keep honouring the buffer_initial_length option. An over-broad fix (forcing FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE on every buffer, flushing on every append, or dropping the stack->heap copy of the buffered prefix) changes that output/identity behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: io streaming versus generating the same object without an io (only the io path is affected)
a short document prefix (<512 bytes, left unflushed in the stack buffer) followed by a single append of 15872-16382 bytes - the only shape that overflows
a single append larger than FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE (16383), which takes the capacity-doubling path
repeated growth/flush cycles over a large document (many small appends; safe in the pinned code)
buffer_initial_length option values (0, negative, custom) which only apply to the non-io path at the pinned commit

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third streaming entry point (e.g. a fragment or streaming writer) that copies this five-line `char stack_buffer[FBUFFER_STACK_SIZE]; FBuffer buffer = { .io = ... }; fbuffer_stack_init(...)` block
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the setup block is already duplicated verbatim at generator.c:1310-1314 and 1872-1876, so a maintainer adding another io-taking generator function would copy it with the stack buffer again and reproduce the bug.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new bulk-append helper (like fbuffer_append_str_repeat) that reserves `repeat * len` via fbuffer_inc_capa and writes in a loop, but is used on an io buffer before the first growth
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already has three reserve-then-write helpers, and each of them relies on fbuffer_inc_capa accounting for fb->len; a new one written against the io fast path would inherit the same len-blind assumption.

O9_family: heap buffer overflow from an incorrect buffer-size calculation (CWE-122 / CWE-131 / CWE-787)

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 3.3 headers with mkmf/extconf (ext/json/ext/generator/extconf.rb), a C99 compiler, optional SSE2/NEON SIMD; JSON_DEBUG=1 builds reservation assertions
O10_build.project_tests: test/json/json_common_interface_test.rb:263 (test_dump_in_io: StringIO streaming, `assert_same io, JSON.dump([1], io)`, large-object streaming) and test/json/json_generator_test.rb:432 (buffer_initial_length), run with `rake test` or `ruby -Ilib -Itest`; no existing test exercises the stack-buffer-to-IO-heap promotion window.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Take the commit title literally and only stop passing the stack buffer in the two generator entry points' FBuffer initialisation, leaving the len-blind `requested < fb->capa` guard in fbuffer_do_inc_capa unfixed.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/json/truffle_ruby/generator.rb and java/src/json/ext/Generator.java are separate generator implementations for other runtimes, untouched by the fix and using GC-managed buffers (no FBuffer sink); not pursued.
ext/json/ext/parser/parser.c has no FBuffer and is a separate area from this advisory; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell/du available); the tree is 125 files with no large source subtree, so tiny_repo is judged from the listing rather than an exact size.
The overflow window (a prefix buffered in the 512-byte stack buffer plus a first-growth append of 15872-16382 bytes) is derived by reading the code, not by running it; no execution was permitted.

Whether the grading harness builds with ASAN/valgrind is unknown. JSON_DEBUG's assertions (ext/json/ext/fbuffer/fbuffer.h:53-62) only compare consumed against the reserved count, which matches here, so a plain build may not fail deterministically on the up-to-511-byte overrun.
